sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Decision curve analysis to evaluate the clinical benefit of prediction models》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Abstract · abstract-1-2】Prediction models are typically evaluated in terms of their accuracy: discrimination (area-under-the-curve [AUC] or concordance index) and calibration (a plot of predicted vs. observed risk).

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】But it can be hard to know how high an AUC has to be in order to be "high enough" to warrant use of a prediction model, or how much miscalibration would be disqualifying.

evidence.text: Prediction models are typically evaluated in terms of their accuracy: discrimination (area-under-the-curve [AUC] or concordance index) and calibration (a plot of predicted vs. observed risk).
But it can be hard to know how high an AUC has to be in order to be "high enough" to warrant use of a prediction model, or how much miscalibration would be disqualifying.
